name: Creature Type Origination Methods and Compatibility
scope: General tabletop origination-method defaults, not an executable Character Origins builder or automatic Species/Ancestry grants.

methodDefinitions.name: Biological reproduction
methodDefinitions.description: A living contributor reproduces by an appropriate biological process; the specific process establishes contributions and prerequisites.

methodDefinitions.name: Plant reproduction
methodDefinitions.description: A distinct Plant origination family that can later define pollination, fertilization, spores, or other plant/fungal processes without assuming animal reproduction.

methodDefinitions.name: Construct assembly
methodDefinitions.description: Materials, design, assembly, and any animating force may play different input roles; creator Species traits are not inherited automatically.

methodDefinitions.name: Elemental manifestation
methodDefinitions.description: Elemental beings may coalesce or manifest from elemental or magical sources; specific processes and component roles are defined by the Species or scenario.

methodDefinitions.name: Spawning
methodDefinitions.description: A nonbiological or otherwise distinct spawning process, with its own input requirements and permitted contributors.

methodDefinitions.name: Division
methodDefinitions.description: Creation through separation of an existing creature or mass, subject to individual creature rules.

methodDefinitions.name: Reanimation
methodDefinitions.description: An existing creature or remains becomes animated through an applicable process; this does not imply biological descent.

methodDefinitions.name: Transformation
methodDefinitions.description: An existing individual changes its configuration or type under an explicit effect or process; existing Heritage is not erased by relabeling.

methodDefinitions.name: Rite of Rebirth
methodDefinitions.description: A qualifying ritual completely replaces the current Species and Ancestry configuration of an existing creature. It is a specific transformation, not biological reproduction, contributor mixing, or a second individual being born.

methodInheritance.rule: A creature type inherits the nearest explicitly authored list along its type-parent chain. Its own list replaces that default; a Species or Ancestry may explicitly add, restrict, or replace applicable methods.
methodInheritance.emptyListMeans: no general method granted; not an absolute ban

compatibility.biologicalAndPlantReproduction: A contributing creature must support the selected reproductive method or be specifically authorized to participate. Different creature types are not inherently incompatible.
compatibility.specificProcessRequirements: Apply the selected process's contributor roles, number of required inputs, and explicit restrictions, including full-set conditions; do not assume exactly two parents.
compatibility.unknown: Unsupported or undocumented combinations remain unresolved under first-party rules, not categorically forbidden.
compatibility.explicitRestrictions: A type, Species, Ancestry, or origination process can impose a more specific restriction.
compatibility.dmOverride: Any origination compatibility default, restriction, or method requirement can be replaced by an authorized DM/table ruling, including new contributor arrangements and otherwise unsupported combinations; record the table-effective decision without changing first-party defaults.
compatibility.distinctFromManifestation: Compatibility and origination do not automatically grant source characteristics, choose an effective creature type, or establish mechanical coherence.

reviewNotes: First-party method support is intentionally permissive and incomplete; an individual creature can have an exception and a type can have multiple methods.
Plant reproduction is a distinct method, not the generic biological-reproduction method.
Genies remain Elementals; their potential for biological offspring is Species-specific and does not require all Elementals to support biological reproduction.
Removing Monstrous Humanoid and True Elemental does not automatically change preexisting monster stat blocks, material-body properties, or targeting semantics of other types.
The general rules remain understandable and usable at the table without Rules Core software.
Rite of Rebirth is a post-origination complete replacement operation, offered by a qualifying specific Rite or a DM exception, not by default to all members of any creature type.
Ancestry acquisitionMethods may restrict default acquisition to a validated Rite; current exceptional Dragonborn concepts are not yet native selectable Ancestry definitions.
DM/table decisions can override any Origin rule at any level; first-party descriptions and validation are defaults, never an exhaustive restriction on the table's allowed mechanics.

methodAvailability.typeDefault: Creature-type originationMethods provide ordinary available methods, but are not an exhaustive list of rituals, transformations, or DM-authorized exceptions.
methodAvailability.explicitProcess: An authored Rite can authorize its transformation independently of the subject's creature-type default originationMethods. A method's existence in the catalog alone does not grant access to a Rite or its target Ancestry.
methodAvailability.dmOverride: The DM can permit, remove, modify, or add any origination method, contribution role, requirement, or source restriction at the specified table scope, including overriding any creature-type default.

riteOfRebirth.subject: existing-creature

targetAcquisition.restrictedAncestryRule: An Ancestry authored with acquisitionMethods containing only rite-of-rebirth is unavailable through ordinary initial Species/Ancestry selection or ordinary mixed-Heritage candidate selection under the first-party defaults. An authorized DM/table ruling can allow another acquisition path or otherwise change this requirement.
targetAcquisition.unspecifiedField: Existing Ancestries without an acquisitionMethods restriction retain their prior selection behavior; merely defining the Rite does not restrict them.
targetAcquisition.specificRitesMayRequire: Explicit participants, materials, permissions, prerequisites, and a specific target Species/Ancestry; no universal ritual procedure is imposed.

riteOfRebirth.doesNotAuthorize: The Rite's listing does not grant target access, expose restricted extraordinary traits in ordinary mixed-Heritage pools, define ritual costs, or create native exceptional Ancestry records.
riteOfRebirth.dmOverride: Every Rite rule, including participant/prerequisite requirements, acquisition gates, full replacement behavior, which grants are retained or changed, and even whether a particular transformation counts as a Rite, may be changed by an explicit DM/table ruling. Complete replacement remains the first-party default, not an immutable engine restriction.

dmOverridePolicy.rule: Every first-party classification, inherited default, process, requirement, restriction, eligibility rule, characteristic, selection, reconciliation decision, manifestation, reconstruction, and transformation outcome may be replaced, supplemented, or waived by an explicit DM/table decision. An override is not limited to granting exceptions to prohibitions.
dmOverridePolicy.scope: All stages and nested operations of Character Origins, including creature-type membership and hierarchy, available origination methods, source/input roles, contributor counts, biological and nonbiological compatibility, transmitted characteristics, choices and parameters, resulting creature type, character grants, Rite of Rebirth acquisition requirements and replacement behavior, and custom/homebrew definitions. These examples do not form a whitelist.
tableProcedure: Identify the published default or unresolved question.
State the table's alternative decision, including any new or modified characteristics necessary to use it.
Apply that decision within the scope chosen by the DM, then construct or validate the resulting Origin under the effective table rules.

recordWhenAutomated.authority: A DM or other actor authorized under the table's campaign permissions.
recordWhenAutomated.scope: The campaign, character, creature, creation event, or narrower context to which the decision applies.
recordWhenAutomated.target: The affected rule, entity, stage, or whole configuration; may include new table-authored content.
recordWhenAutomated.effectiveDecision: The rule or resulting outcome adopted by the table, including a custom mechanic where needed.

resolution.precedence: Within its declared scope, an authorized DM/table decision takes precedence over conflicting first-party defaults; outside that scope the published defaults remain unchanged.
resolution.firstPartyCatalog: An override changes the effective table rules, not the global published catalog or the rules another campaign uses.
resolution.unresolved: Unknown mechanics may be defined by an explicit table decision. Do not silently infer mechanics or treat a missing rule as automatic approval.
resolution.consistency: Evaluate the whole resulting configuration against the table's effective rules, not only the unmodified first-party defaults. Any remaining contradictions can themselves be adjudicated.
resolution.softwareAuthorization: Game-rule overrides do not bypass application authentication, ownership permissions, access controls, or data validation for safely representing the decision.
resolution.runtimeStatus: Declarative policy only; a trusted override authoring, storage, precedence, and grant-evaluation executor is not implemented in this content change.
